messages:
maria (runtime): quick heads-up — I ran a focused profile on the decode path with heavy tool/function-calling traffic and we’re seeing weird queue pileups when stop-token/tool pauses happen.
aj: can you paste the profile? curious if it’s batching or kernel selection.
maria (runtime): pasted below. TL;DR: requests that do toolcall -> pause often hold a token-budget slot for much longer than expected and cause the continuous-batcher to form very uneven batches.

maria (runtime): profile snippet: 
```
time   func                          cpu%   notes
0.0-1.2 decode_loop                  54%    waiting on KV lock (fragmented)
1.2-1.4 kernel_select                18%    fallback to fp32 for certain GELU kernels
1.4-1.7 kv_cache_get                 12%    long-tail for partial-evict entries
1.7-2.0 queue_wait                    9%    toolcall pause holding queue token
```

gina: hmm kv fragmentation + kernel fallback — that explains the 2.1x P99 regression I saw on staging for chat-tool routes after the 0.24.0 runtime change.
sudhir: where is the lock contention coming from? my guess is concurrent evicts during batching amplification.
maria (runtime): exact. evict path runs on the same thread for small caches; when a toolcall pause returns, we hit a spike of small cache writes and that serializes kernel selection and batch draining.
aj: do we have telemetry to correlate toolcall=true with increased kernel_select fp32 counts?
maria (runtime): added a quick debug metric: `kernel_fp32_fallback_count` + `toolcall_pause_active`. Early data shows routes with >15% toolcall rate have 3x fallback rate.

aj: possible mitigations?
sudhir: ideas: (1) separate queue for pause-prone requests so they don't block the regular fast-path, (2) token-budget shrink for toolcall batch membership (so they don't grab long windows), (3) preselect kernel earlier before batch flush to avoid late fallback when KV hits.
maria (runtime): i prototyped (2) and (3). setting token_budget_target=16 for toolcall-tagged requests reduced batch holding time by ~60% in the microbench. preselecting kernel on enqueue avoided late fp32 fallback in ~75% of cases.

gina: did that change affect end-to-end quality or latency for short-invocations?
maria (runtime): negligible quality impact; p50 improved, p99 improved for mixed workloads. downside: slightly more small batches which raises GPU util ~3%.

aj: tradeoff seems reasonable for hosted routes. for Dedicated customers with strict throughput SLOs might be different.
sudhir: question on KV: can we make cache writes asynchronous on pause-resume? decouple evict path from main decode thread?
maria (runtime): that’s the long-term fix. asynchronous eviction + background compaction should reduce fragmentation. I sketched a patch to pump evicts onto a low-priority worker. early numbers promising but needs safety checks.

deploy-bot: deploy request submitted for branch `queue-shaping/toolcall-budget` (PR #4592) — CI green.

ajn: small nit — name the new metric `toolcall_pause_queue_time_ms` so ops can alert.

ops-bot: alert rule suggestion: if toolcall_pause_queue_time_ms P95 > 200ms for 5min -> page oncall.

maria (runtime): next steps I propose:
- merge the token_budget_target tweak behind feature flag for hosted (A/B).
- enable pre-kernel-selection on enqueue and add assert telemetry.
- instrument `toolcall_pause` tag end-to-end in Console dashboards.
- prototype async evict worker (separate RFC).

gina: +1. can you assign owner and ETA?
maria (runtime): assigning to me for the feature-flag rollout (ETA: 1 week). sudhir owns the async-evict RFC (ETA: 3w). aj to add dashboard tiles and alert (ETA: 2 days).

aj: will also add a short smoke test to ensure Dedicated configs can opt-out of the budget change.
sudhir: will check Dedicated perf implications; we may need a separate knob for auto-scaling pools.

maria (runtime): thanks — I’ll push the PR and post perf numbers after a canary run. for now, signal if anyone sees regressions on staging chat-tool. :pray:
aj: noted. will keep an eye and run the long-tail synthetic again overnight.
